ai.overview: The Colorado Avalanche put their Belt Holders championship on the line for the first time in this reign when they host the Calgary Flames on Halloween night. Colorado claimed the belt in their most recent outing and will look to begin a defensive streak, while Calgary seeks to reclaim a belt they've held 68 times previously in the lineal championship's history. The all-time series between these franchises is remarkably tight at 85-83-20 across 188 meetings.
key_matchups: Colorado's recent offensive surge (5-2, 6-3 wins in their last three victories) against a Calgary team shut out 4-0 in their most recent game
Home ice advantage for the Avalanche, who have dominated this season's series with victories of 7-3, 3-1, and 9-2
Calgary's four-game winning streak before their Edmonton loss versus Colorado's inconsistent 2-3 stretch prior to their latest win
ai.betting_angles: The Elo model strongly favors Colorado, and recent head-to-head results support that assessment with the Avalanche winning all four meetings this season by comfortable margins including a 9-2 drubbing. Colorado's 7-6 record edges Calgary's 5-7 mark, and the home side just posted a convincing 5-2 victory while the Flames were blanked 4-0 in their last outing. Calgary had looked sharp with four straight wins before that Edmonton loss, but their struggles this season and inability to solve Colorado recently suggest this will be an uphill battle.
ai.prediction_writeup: Colorado has owned this matchup in 2026, winning all four meetings including three blowouts, and they'll be defending the belt at home where they just put up five goals against New Jersey. Calgary arrives off a shutout loss and sits two games below .500, while the Avalanche have the better record and clear Elo advantage. The Flames have held the belt 68 times before and know what's at stake, but the recent head-to-head history is too lopsided to ignore. Colorado keeps the belt with a multi-goal victory in what should be a relatively comfortable home win.
